trigger: A single sentence chains several distinct operations or claims across semicolons and subordinate clauses (e.g., spec, exception, mechanism, and hedge at once), so the reader must hold the whole chain together.
gap_fix: Let one operation or fact advance per sentence and split compound logic across separate sentences, the way the exemplars stop the sentence after one operation, rather than threading several into one chain.

trigger: Several parallel findings or definitions (e.g., multiple measures each with its coefficient and p-value) are strung together across semicolons inside one sentence.
gap_fix: Give each enumerated item its own sentence the way the exemplars do, rather than packing the parallel list into one semicolon-spliced period the reader must segment.

trigger: A head noun is preceded by a stack of piled adjectives and nouns the reader must unzip (dense multi-modifier descriptors in front of the noun).

trigger: A plainly nameable quantity is introduced through a relational descriptor layered over it (e.g., 'the discriminating window is the gap') rather than by its plain name.
gap_fix: Name the concrete coefficient or variable plainly the way the exemplars do, dropping the added relational-abstraction layer over the plain named quantity.

trigger: Set-builder notation with braced members and multi-index subscripts is embedded inline in running prose, so the reader parses set membership and triple subscripts mid-sentence.
gap_fix: Define each variable in plain expanded prose with its name attached, one clause per variable, the way the exemplars unpack symbols after an equation, rather than asking the reader to decode braces and subscripts inline.

trigger: Multiple hedges are compounded inside one sentence — a counterfactual condition, its consequence, and a re-labeling stacked in sequence.
